With an RPC client, `start()` takes the handlers for the requests and events of the bundle, so that they are registered before the bundle can send any.

Changed in v0.3.6: the generated code depends on the releases of `bare-rpc` that support cancellation: `bare-rpc` 2.x and `bare-abort-controller` in the bundle and in a JavaScript harness, and `bare-rpc-swift` 3.x, `bare-rpc-kotlin` 0.6.x, or `bare-rpc` 0.3.x for Python in a harness in those languages. See [Changes in v2.0.0](/bare/reference/bare/modules/bare-rpc#changes-in-v200) on the `bare-rpc` page.

For `bare-kit`, that's `bare-kit-swift` or `bare-kit-kotlin`. Changed in v0.3.7: it links bare-kit-swift `from: "2.3.0"` and bare-kit-kotlin `v0.2.+`, which build Bare Kit 3.1.0. Earlier releases linked bare-kit-swift with a `from:` requirement, which also resolves to 2.3.0, and an exact bare-kit-kotlin release, usually `v0.2.2`, which builds Bare Kit 3.0.1. See [Bundled Bare version](/bare/reference/bare/bare-kit#bundled-bare-version).
